sources.headline: Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees to US call to resume Ukraine peace talks
sources.text: Witkoff described the latest talks as "constructive", while Kushner, who was participating via a video link, said: "There is still hard work ahead, but we have a real opportunity to move beyond this war and build a framework for lasting peace, security, and prosperity for generations to come."The talks were held amid a growing row between Ukraine and the US. Trump has said it is time for Ukraine to get a new president, and most recently "for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine".He has blamed Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries for fuel prices which have been rising since the start of the US-led war on Iran.He was also heavily criticised by Democratic and some Republican lawmakers after lifting sanctions on Russia - allowing it to release tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace".That was despite signing legislation to authorise fresh US sanctions and tariffs on nations that import Russian oil and gas just weeks earlier.Zelensky - and Ukraine's European allies - criticised Trump's move.Last week, Kyiv accused Washington of withholding critical intelligence to warn Ukrainians about incoming Russian ballistic missile launches, resulting in many civilian deaths. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday rejected such accusations as "scandalous", and Zelensky said after the Oslo talks that intelligence sharing "works now".Ukraine's military has also complained of speed restrictions to the US satellite internet network Starlink, which constricted its ability to use drones to conduct strikes against Russia.US officials have denied having requested such a slowdown and a bipartisan group of US senators has called for an urgent investigation.

sources.headline: Russia bombards Kyiv with missiles hours after agreeing to resume talks with Ukraine
sources.text:
Russia has carried out a massive “demonstrative” attack on Ukraine, bombarding Kyiv with ballistic missiles just hours after Vladimir Putin said he had agreed to resume trilateral negotiations after talks with the US envoy Steve Witkoff.Overnight, Moscow pounded the Ukrainian capital, killing at least two people and wounding 22, including four children. Targets included the southern bridge over the Dnipro River, civilian houses, energy infrastructure, an ambulance station, office buildings and a clinic.The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said three of the missiles carried cluster warheads. One struck the Pecherskyi district, damaging several historic structures, including a monastery.“This is another extraordinarily revealing strike – revealing, because it was no accident,” Zelenskyy said. “The choice of weapon was deliberate; the choice of target area was deliberate, and so was the intent to inflict as much loss and damage on civilians as possible.”He said the strikes showed Russia was not serious about peace, adding: “Almost immediately after another round of talks, Russia launched a pointed attack. This means there has been no real change in its attitude toward everything that is happening.”Overnight, Moscow pounded the Ukrainian capital, killing at least two people and wounding 22, including four children. Photograph: Vladislav Musienko/AFP/Getty ImagesDuring negotiations on Wednesday in St Petersburg, Witkoff lavished praise on Putin, who was sitting across the table. “You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian. You are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that,” Witkoff said.In a social media post after the strikes in the early hours of Thursday, Zelenskyy issued a sardonic reply: “Three waves of ballistic missiles have been launched at Kyiv by Russian ‘humanitarians’ since yesterday evening. They used 21 missiles.”Zelenskyy said he was grateful to those among Ukraine’s western partners who saw “the situation for what it is” and “acknowledged the reality” that the Kremlin had little intention of stopping its war. He called for stronger air defences, Patriot interceptors that could bring down enemy missiles, and more sanctions against Moscow.Ukraine’s foreign minister, ⁠Andrii Sybiha, ⁠added that “appeasement, ⁠servility ​and flattery” ‌would ‌not ‌stop Russian aggression.Downing Street said it did not recognise Witkoff’s description of Putin, pointing out that the Russian president had killed “thousands” of Ukrainians and his own frontline soldiers.On Wednesday, the Kremlin foreign affairs adviser Yuri Ushakov said Putin had agreed “in principle” to resume three-way negotiations involving Russia, the US and Ukraine after 10 November, a week after the US midterm elections. In reality, Russia’s intention is to destroy Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in the coming weeks, leaving millions in the dark and cold, officials in Kyiv believe.According to Zelenskyy, the US has resumed intelligence warnings of Russian missile attacks. The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that Trump called Elon Musk to ask him to reverse the slowdown of Starshield, the military version of Musk’s Starlink internet satellite system, which had left Ukraine unable to intercept enemy drones or carry out mid-range battlefield strikes. Some Ukrainian officials reportedly told the Journal that the system had been working marginally better since the call, but others said it was still heavily restricted.The New York Times reported that when the slowdown was imposed last week, dozens of armed drones heading to Russian military targets fell from the sky. The video feeds streaming their flight paths suddenly went fuzzy as the connection with Starshield was lost, the paper said.Vladimir, the commander of an air-defence unit protecting Kyiv, said the US restrictions had hampered his unit’s ability to intercept Russian drones. “Of course it’s hindering us. Our drones can no longer reach the speeds needed to intercept enemy targets,” he said, adding that he felt betrayed by Washington.The decision to cripple Ukraine’s successful drone programme came amid the most serious row between Washington and Kyiv since Russia’s full-scale invasion nearly five years ago. It began after Trump announced he was lifting sanctions on Russian diesel, to lower US fuel prices, a move that Zelenskyy criticised as “weak”.Witkoff calls Putin a ‘humanitarian’ after release of jailed American – videoThe Trump administration denies it is deliberately helping the Russians. But European diplomats concede that the US appears to have switched sides. Ukrainian civilians are dying as a result, they say.Russia, meanwhile, said it had shot down hundreds of Ukrainian drones launched in overnight attacks. One man ⁠was ⁠killed ​and another was ⁠wounded as a ⁠result ​of ‌a Ukrainian aerial strike in Russia’s Belgorod region, local ‌authorities said.Details also emerged of a Ukrainian counterattack through a tunnel in the north-eastern city of Kupiansk, which Russia partly occupies. As part of Operation Veles, the Khartia corps carried out the world’s first underground counteroffensive, advancing 15km into enemy rear lines.“We observed how the enemy operates underground and studied their methods. The Russians intended to use gas pipelines to infiltrate the rear of our forces. So, we went underground ourselves,” Khartia’s commander, Brig Gen Ihor Obolienskyi, told Ukrainian media.The Ukrainian soldiers crawled 15km through tunnels – without communication, GPS or light – having developed their own navigation and life-support technologies in advance. About 100 Russians were killed in the operation, and 30 taken prisoner, the Khartia corps said.
Luke Harding’s Betrayal: Trump, Putin and the New Age of Conquest is published by Guardian Faber

‘No change’ in Russia’s attitude on war shown by deadly attacks, Zelensky says

Russia’s latest attacks on Ukraine show there has been “no real change” in Moscow’s attitude towards the war, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Thursday. The deadly strikes came just hours after Russian President Vladimir Putin told US envoy Steve Witkoff his country was ready to resume trilateral talks with Washington and Kyiv.

Issued on: 22/10/2026 - 18:43

  3 min
Reading time
Share
By:
FRANCE 24
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky at a meeting with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham at 10 Downing Street in London on October 14, 2026. © Henry Nicholls, AFP

Ukraine on Thursday accused Russia of failing to change its position on the war by firing a wave of ballistic missiles just after US envoy Steve Witkoff met President Vladimir Putin to discuss the resumption of peace talks.

Air raid sirens sounded throughout the night and into the day in Kyiv, where two people were killed and more than 30 other people wounded, city authorities said.

Two women aged 50 and 60 were killed and dozens more people were wounded in an attack on a crowded market in the eastern city of Lozova. Two were wounded in the Moscow region after Ukraine launched its own large-scale drone attack.

The strikes came after the Kremlin said it was willing to restart trilateral talks with Kyiv and Washington next month, but dismissed new ideas brought by Witkoff that were developed with European countries and Ukraine.

In all, a dozen Ukrainian regions were hit overnight, including residential houses, energy sites, shops, cafes and a monastery damaged in Kyiv, where strikes have intensified before winter sets in.

Read moreUkraine’s Pavlohrad refuses to yield to Putin despite unrelenting bombardment

All families and children were told to evacuate the frontline towns of Kramatorsk and neighbouring Sloviansk in the east after a spate of attacks killed dozens of civilians.

Zelensky said the onslaught began “almost immediately” after Witkoff and Putin held hours-long talks in Saint Petersburg, scoffing at US President Donald Trump’s envoy’s description of the Russian leader as a “humanitarian”.

“This means there has been no real change in its attitude towards everything that is happening,” he added.

Emboldened

Ukraine has repeatedly called on its allies, including the United States, to supply it with advanced US-made Patriot interceptors to shoot down missiles and fast-moving attack drones.

Zelensky warned of more strikes to come and suggested that Moscow – emboldened by an easing of sanctions pressure – was “clearly taking advantage of the slowdown in air-defence supplies from our partners”, in a clear nod to Washington.

In Brussels, NATO said it was allowing Ukraine to buy weapons through the alliance’s central procurement agency on a “case-by-case basis”.

Trump sought an optimistic tone as his envoy returned from Russia and on Wednesday said negotiators were “maybe now the closest we’ve been” to ending the war.

But in Kyiv and European capitals, hopes for a breakthrough were slim, with many worried the White House was siding with Moscow.

Cover image: Russian President Vladimir Putin shakes hands with US special envoy Steve Witkoff during a meeting at the Constantine Palace in Saint Petersburg, Russia, October 21, 2026. via REUTERS - Gavriil Grigorov
06:27

Zelensky accused Russia of deliberately targeting civilians in Kyiv, including with cluster munitions, which disperse in the air, showering dozens of smaller explosive devices or bomblets indiscriminately over a large area.

Human Rights Watch in August reported an apparent increase in the use of the weapons, which are fired in rockets and missiles or dropped from aircraft. Doing so could be a war crime, it added.

Moscow invaded Ukraine in February 2022 in what it hoped would be a swift attack to topple Zelensky and seize land.

Instead it has become bogged down in Europe’s biggest conflict since World War II. Hundreds of thousands have been killed, millions forced from their homes and much of eastern and southern Ukraine destroyed.

Talks

Zelensky met Witkoff in Norway on Tuesday as relations between Kyiv and Washington plunged to their worst state since Trump publicly berated Zelensky in the Oval Office in February 2025.

Read moreUkraine ‘losing people and time’, Zelensky says after Oslo talks

In recent days, Trump has blocked new sanctions on Russia, struck a deal to buy Russian diesel, and called for the Ukrainian leader to be replaced.

Zelensky has backed resuming trilateral talks – several rounds of which over the last 18 months have failed to move the sides closer to a deal.

Russia is demanding Ukraine pull out of territory in the eastern Donetsk region that it still controls, and wants sweeping political and military restrictions on the size of its army and Western alliances.

Ukraine rejects the demands as tantamount to a capitulation that would leave it exposed to a fresh attack.

Moscow said that a summit between Trump, Putin and China’s Xi Jinping was being prepared in China for next month, with Europeans and Ukraine worrying a deal could be struck over their heads.

Witkoff called his talks with Putin “constructive” but “there is still important work left to do” and technical-level talks would continue between all three sides.

Putin has consistently rejected face-to-face talks with Zelensky and insisted Moscow intends to seize the rest of eastern Ukraine – either through a deal or on the battlefield.

(FRANCE 24 with AFP)
